fixed_comments.original:
## Investigation Complete

### Reports Created
- Release report: `docs/releases/v3.0.0/features/opensearch/lucene-10-upgrade.md`
- Feature report: `docs/features/opensearch/lucene-10-upgrade.md`

### Summary
OpenSearch 3.0.0 upgrades from Apache Lucene 9.12.1 to Lucene 10.1.0, a major dependency upgrade that brings significant performance improvements and requires JDK 21 as the minimum runtime.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- **Lucene Version**: 9.12.1 → 10.1.0
- **JDK Requirement**: Minimum JDK raised from 11 to 21
- **I/O Parallelism**: New async I/O API for improved disk operations
- **Search Parallelism**: Logical partitions within segments for parallel search
- **Sparse Indexing**: Block-based indexing with min/max values for query optimization
- **k-NN/Vector Search**: Improved HNSW implementation and parallelized execution

### Breaking Changes
- `dutch_kp` and `lovins` stemmers removed
- `german2` stemmer merged into `german`
- `TotalHits.value` changed to `TotalHits.value()` (field to method)
- Plugins using Lucene APIs directly may require updates

### Resources Used
- PR: [#16366](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/16366) - Update to Apache Lucene 10 for 3.0.0
- Issue: [#11415](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/issues/11415) - Feature request
- Blog: [OpenSearch 3.0: What to Expect](https://opensearch.org/blog/opensearch-3-0-what-to-expect/)
- Docs: [Breaking Changes Guide](https://github.com/opensearch-project/opensearch-build/issues/5243)

### Features (236)

Key features include:
- **OpenSearch Core**: HTTP/2 support, Views, Pull-based Ingestion (Kafka/Kinesis), Star Tree aggregations, Arrow Flight RPC, GRPC endpoints, Scale to zero support
- **ML Commons**: MCP support, Plan/Execute/Reflect Agent, Function calling, Async agent execution
- **Neural Search**: Semantic highlighter, Z Score normalization, Hybrid query improvements, Semantic field mapper
- **k-NN**: Remote Vector Index Build, Memory-optimized search mode, Explain API support
- **SQL**: Calcite engine framework, PPL join/subquery commands, New UDFs

### Enhancements (87)

Key enhancements across dashboards-assistant, security, anomaly-detection, flow-framework, ml-commons, neural-search, observability, query insights, and more.

### Bug Fixes (526)

Extensive bug fixes across all repositories including build fixes, security patches, CI/CD improvements, and compatibility updates.

### Deprecations (44)

Removal of legacy code, deprecated settings, and version constants.

3. Investigate: `python run.py investigate --issue {number}`

## Investigation Complete: Star Tree Index (#16)

### Reports Created
- Release report: `docs/releases/v3.0.0/features/opensearch/star-tree-enhancements.md`
- Feature report: `docs/features/opensearch/star-tree-index.md` (created)

### Summary
Investigated the Star Tree Index enhancements for v3.0.0. Star-tree index is a multi-field index that precomputes aggregations during indexing, significantly reducing query latency for analytics workloads.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- **Keyword and Numeric Terms Aggregations** - Terms aggregations on both keyword and numeric fields can now leverage star-tree optimization
- **Range Aggregations** - Numeric range aggregations with metric sub-aggregations are now supported
- **Boolean Query Support** - Complex boolean queries with MUST and SHOULD clauses can be resolved via star-tree
- **Unsigned Long Support** - The unsigned-long data type is now fully supported in star-tree indexing and search operations

### Performance Highlights
- Metric aggregation on 200M documents: 4.2s → 6.3ms (~667x improvement)
- Date histogram with sum on 120M documents: 13s → 94ms (~138x improvement)

### Resources Used
- PRs: #17165, #17273, #17275, #17941
- Issues: #16551, #16553, #15231, #17267
- Docs: https://docs.opensearch.org/3.0/search-plugins/star-tree-index/
- Blog: https://opensearch.org/blog/the-power-of-star-tree-indexes-supercharging-opensearch-aggregations/

### PR
- #473 (merged)

### Reports Already Exist
- Release report: `docs/releases/v3.0.0/features/opensearch/thread-context-permissions.md` ✅
- Feature report: `docs/features/opensearch/thread-context-permissions.md` ✅

### Summary
Thread Context Permissions is a security enhancement in v3.0.0 that protects sensitive methods in OpenSearch's `ThreadContext` class using Java Security Manager permissions. This is a **breaking change** for plugins.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- New `ThreadContextPermission` class in `org.opensearch.secure_sm` package
- New `ThreadContextAccess` helper class for privileged operations
- Three methods now require explicit permissions:
  - `markAsSystemContext()` - marks thread as system context, bypassing user auth
  - `stashWithOrigin(String)` - stashes context and sets action origin
  - `stashAndMergeHeaders(Map)` - stashes context and merges headers
- Plugins must declare permissions in `plugin-security.policy` file

### Resources Used
- PR: [#15016](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/15016) - markAsSystemContext permission
- PR: [#15039](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/15039) - stashWithOrigin and stashAndMergeHeaders permissions

### Summary
The HTTP Client Migration feature migrates OpenSearch client transports from Apache HttpComponents/Core 4.x (EOL) to Apache HttpClient/Core 5.x. This is a breaking change that affects all OpenSearch clients (rest-client, RHLC, opensearch-java).

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- Migrated from `org.apache.http` packages to `org.apache.hc` packages
- Updated entity classes: `NByteArrayEntity` → `ByteArrayEntity`, `NStringEntity` → `StringEntity`
- Changed `HttpResponse` to `ClassicHttpResponse`
- Added new dependencies: `httpclient5` (5.1.3) and `httpcore5` (5.1.4)
- `ContentType.getValue()` now returns `String` directly instead of `Header`
- `HttpHost` constructor parameter order changed (protocol first in 5.x)

### Findings

The PRs referenced in this issue (#14283 and #6595) are from the **OpenSearch core** repository, not OpenSearch-Dashboards. The Bulk API changes are server-side changes in the OpenSearch engine.

### Reports Already Exist

The documentation for these changes has already been created in the correct location:

### Summary of Changes

The v3.0.0 Bulk API breaking changes include:

1. **Removal of `batch_size` parameter** ([PR #17801](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/17801))
   - The deprecated `batch_size` parameter has been removed from the `_bulk` API
   - Batch processing for ingest pipelines is now automatic
   - Resolves [Issue #14283](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/issues/14283)

2. **512 byte document ID limit enforcement** ([PR #8039](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/8039))
   - The Bulk API now enforces the 512 byte `_id` size limit
   - Previously, this limit could be bypassed through bulk operations
   - Resolves [Issue #6595](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/issues/6595)

### Summary
OpenSearch 3.0 introduces comprehensive Model Context Protocol (MCP) support in ML Commons, enabling standardized integration between AI agents and external tools. - Feature report: `docs/features/k-nn/lucene-on-faiss.md` (created)

### Summary
Lucene-on-Faiss is a hybrid vector search approach introduced in OpenSearch v3.0.0 that enables vector searches on FAISS HNSW indexes without loading the entire index into memory. This addresses a fundamental limitation of FAISS and allows vector search operations in memory-constrained environments.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- New `index.knn.memory_optimized_search` index setting to enable partial loading
- Java-based implementation using Lucene's HnswGraphSearcher on FAISS index format
- Support for FP32, FP16, and scalar quantized (8-bit) vectors
- Support for L2 and INNER_PRODUCT space types
- New components: `FaissIndex`, `FaissHnswGraph`, `FaissMemoryOptimizedSearcher`, `VectorSearcherFactory`

### Performance Highlights
- For quantized indexes (8x, 16x, 32x), achieves up to 2x throughput improvement over FAISS C++
- Enables running 30GB indexes on 8GB RAM instances
- Slight recall reduction (up to 4.5%) due to Lucene's early termination logic

- RFC: [#2401](https://github.com/opensearch-project/k-NN/issues/2401)

- **Enhanced Explain**: New explain endpoint output showing logical and physical query plans
- **Configuration**: Enable via `plugins.calcite.enabled: true` setting

   - New `GET /_insights/live_queries` endpoint
   - Real-time monitoring of in-flight search queries
   - Supports filtering by node, sorting by latency/cpu/memory, and size limits

   - Auto-expanding replicas (0-2) for high availability
   - Configurable template priority via `search.insights.top_queries.exporter.template_priority`

   - `verbose=false` option for lightweight API responses
   - Omits `task_resource_usages`, `source`, and `phase_latency_map` fields

4. **Skip Profile Queries** (PR #298)
   - Profile queries automatically excluded from Top N queries collection
   - Prevents diagnostic queries from polluting insights data

   - Data integrity improvement for top queries indices

### Summary
This PR (#3488) adds comprehensive documentation for the PPL V3 engine in OpenSearch 3.0.0 Beta. The V3 engine integrates Apache Calcite for enhanced query processing, introducing new PPL commands (join, lookup, subquery) while maintaining backward compatibility through a fallback mechanism.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- **New V3 Engine Architecture**: Apache Calcite integration for query optimization
- **New PPL Commands**: `join`, `lookup`, `subquery` (subsearch) for complex data operations
- **Breaking Changes**: Return type changes for several functions (`timestampdiff`, `regexp`, `count`, etc.)
- **Fallback Mechanism**: Unsupported V3 queries automatically fall back to V2 engine
- **Configuration**: `plugins.calcite.enabled` setting (disabled by default)

### Summary
This batch includes bug fixes and improvements for the Query Insights plugin's local index exporter functionality, focusing on reliability, performance, and single-node domain compatibility.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0 (Batch 2)
- **Fix default exporter settings** (#234): Fixed broken exporter logic after PR #217 that prevented data export to local index; deeply refactored related logic
- **Local index replica count to 0** (#257): Changed default replica count from 1 to 0 so `top_queries-*` indices show green health on single-node domains
- **Improved expired index deletion** (#262): Use ClusterStateRequest with index pattern (`top_queries-*`) instead of scanning all indices, reducing computation and risk
- **Reduced MAX_TOP_N_INDEX_READ_SIZE to 50** (#281): Optimized query retrieval limit with descending latency sort by default
- **Integration tests for exporter and reader** (#267): Added comprehensive test coverage for exporter configuration, search operations, and debug mode

### Summary
This investigation covered the k-NN plugin's derived source handling and codec refactoring changes in OpenSearch 3.0.0. The changes significantly improve storage efficiency and simplify the codebase architecture.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0

**Derived Source Improvements:**
- Migrated from field attributes to segment attributes for storing derived source information
- Changed from filter-based to mask-based approach for better nested document handling
- Potential storage savings of 50%+ for vector-heavy workloads

**Codec Refactoring:**
- Introduced `backwards_codecs` package for managing legacy read-only codecs
- Removed old codecs no longer supported in OpenSearch 3.0
- Simplified `KNNCodecVersion` class to track only the latest version
- Removed `KNNFormatFacade` in favor of direct constructor calls

**Field Mapper Consolidation:**
- Merged `MethodFieldMapper` and `LuceneFieldMapper` into unified `EngineFieldMapper`
- Changed default value for docValues to reduce storage overhead
- Cleaner architecture with three mapper types: EngineFieldMapper, ModelFieldMapper, FlatFieldMapper

**Breaking Changes:**
- NMSLIB engine blocked for new index creation
- Removed deprecated settings: `knn.plugin.enabled`, `index.knn.algo_param.ef_construction`, `index.knn.algo_param.m`, `index.knn.space_type`

### Summary
OpenSearch 3.0.0 introduces server-side HTTP/2 protocol support via the Netty4 transport module. This enables multiplexed request/response handling over a single connection, eliminating head-of-line blocking issues present in HTTP/1.1.

- **h2c support**: HTTP/2 over cleartext without TLS

### Summary
The Extensions Framework in OpenSearch 3.0.0 received significant security enhancements for authentication token handling. Two key features were implemented:

1. **On Behalf Of (OBO) Token Passing** - Extensions can now receive authentication tokens that represent the original user making a request, enabling proper authorization when extensions interact with OpenSearch.

2. **Service Account Tokens** - Extensions receive a dedicated service account token during initialization, allowing them to authenticate as themselves when accessing their reserved system indices.

- Added `OnBehalfOfClaims` class for OBO token claims (audience, subject, expiration)
- Added `issueOnBehalfOfToken()` method to TokenManager interface
- Added `issueServiceAccountToken()` method to TokenManager interface
- Added `serviceAccountHeader` field to `InitializeExtensionRequest`
- ExtensionsManager now requires IdentityService for token generation
- Token encoding changed from standard Base64 to URL-safe Base64

### Summary
OpenSearch 3.0.0 introduces systemd security configurations to strengthen OS-level security. This feature provides process-level sandboxing using native Linux security mechanisms as part of the Java Security Manager (JSM) replacement strategy.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- Hardened systemd unit file (`opensearch.service`) with comprehensive security directives
- seccomp system call filtering to restrict kernel interfaces (`@system-service`, `~@reboot`, `~@swap`)

- Filesystem isolation with `ReadWritePaths` and `ReadOnlyPaths` directives
- Process protection with `PrivateTmp`, `NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem`, `ProtectKernelModules`
- Integration tests (`SystemdIntegTests.java`) validating security configurations

fixed_comments.original:
## Investigation Complete

### Reports Created
- Release report: `docs/releases/v3.0.0/features/opensearch/aggregations.md`
- Feature report: `docs/features/opensearch/aggregation-optimizations.md` (updated)

### Summary
OpenSearch 3.0.0 introduces three key aggregation performance improvements:

1. **Cardinality Aggregation `execution_hint`**: New parameter to control execution mode
   - `ordinals`: Forces OrdinalsCollector (faster but uses more memory)
   - `direct`: Forces DirectCollector (slower but more memory-efficient)
   - Workaround for users experiencing latency regression when upgrading from OS 2.x

2. **Multi-Term Aggregation Performance**: 
   - 7-10 second latency reduction on benchmark queries
   - Reduced memory allocations by eliminating unnecessary deep copies
   - Optimized iterator usage to avoid allocation overhead

3. **Numeric Term Aggregation Sorting**:
   - Eliminated redundant heap sort when final reduce order is by key
   - PriorityQueue ensures topN buckets by count; sorting by count before key-based final reduce was unnecessary

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- New `execution_hint` parameter for cardinality aggregation
- Multi-term aggregation: Removed deep copy of composite keys, optimized single-valued field handling
- Numeric term aggregation: Skip heap sort when order is not by key

OpenSearch 3.0.0 introduces significant improvements to segment replication, including shard-level stats computation, improved lag metrics accuracy, configurable checkpoint retry timeout, and increased segment counter step size for replica promotion.

### Summary
Rule-Based Auto-Tagging is a new feature in OpenSearch v3.0.0 that automatically assigns feature values (such as workload group IDs) to incoming queries based on specified attributes like index patterns. This enables automatic query categorization without manual intervention.

| `Attribute` | Interface for rule attributes (e.g., `index_pattern`) |
| `FeatureType` | Interface defining feature categories (e.g., `workload_group`) |
| `AutoTaggingRegistry` | Central registry for managing feature types |
| `DefaultAttributeValueStore` | Patricia Trie-based implementation |
| `InMemoryRuleProcessingService` | Service for rule management and label evaluation |

### Summary
OpenSearch 3.0.0 introduces several query performance optimizations that significantly improve search latency and aggregation performance. The changes include faster terms_query execution, approximate match_all queries with sort optimization, extended filter rewrite optimization for sub-aggregations, and disabled scoring for keyword term searches by default.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- **Faster terms_query** (#17714): Avoids re-sorting when terms are already in order by passing pre-sorted terms to TermInSetQuery
- **ApproximateMatchAllQuery** (#17772): Short-circuits match_all queries with sorts after collecting 10,000 documents
- **Sub-aggregation filter rewrite** (#17447): Extends filter rewrite optimization to work with nested aggregations (700-1500ms improvement on dense data)
- **Disabled keyword term scoring** (#17889): Eliminates BM25 scoring overhead for keyword field searches (20x faster: 10ms vs 200ms)

### Summary
OpenSearch v3.0.0 introduces two key improvements to tiered caching:

1. **Single Cache Manager for Disk Caches** - Reduces CPU overhead by using a single `EhcacheDiskCacheManager` per cache type instead of creating separate cache managers for each disk cache segment.

2. **Took-Time Policy Extended to Heap Tier** - The minimum took-time threshold policy now guards both the heap tier and disk tier, preventing cheap queries from flooding the heap cache.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- New `EhcacheDiskCacheManager` class manages all disk caches via a single `PersistentCacheManager`
- Shared thread pool sized between 2 and 1.5× CPU cores (previously each cache had its own pool)
- New setting `indices.requests.cache.tiered_spillover.policies.took_time.threshold` (default: 0ms) for heap tier
- Existing disk tier setting unchanged for backwards compatibility

### Summary
Fixed interval refresh task scheduling is a new feature in OpenSearch v3.0.0 that ensures consistent intervals between index refreshes. This is part of the broader effort to improve data freshness for remote store indexes (Meta Issue #17776).

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- New cluster setting `cluster.index.refresh.fixed_interval_scheduling.enabled` (default: false)
- Enhanced `AbstractAsyncTask` to track last run time and calculate dynamic sleep durations
- Staggered initial refresh starts to prevent concurrent refreshes across shards (dense shard packing)
- Dynamic sleep calculation: if refresh takes longer than interval, next refresh is scheduled immediately; otherwise, sleep for remaining time

- Feature report: `docs/features/opensearch/source-field-matching.md` (created)

### Summary
This release item introduces a performance optimization for `_source` field filtering in OpenSearch v3.0.0. When filtering source fields using simple field names (without wildcards or dot-paths), OpenSearch now uses a HashSet-based matching approach instead of the more complex automaton-based matching.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- Added `hasNoWildcardsOrDots()` helper method to detect simple field names
- Added `createSetBasedFilter()` for O(1) HashSet-based field matching
- Added `createAutomatonFilter()` to encapsulate the existing automaton logic
- Automatic selection between HashSet and automaton strategies based on field name patterns

### Problem Solved
Previously, when fetching source fields with many long field names, Lucene would throw a `TooComplexToDeterminizeException` because the automaton-based matching created a complex union between linear automata. The new HashSet optimization avoids this by using simple set membership checks for simple field names.

### Summary
OpenSearch 3.0.0 migrates from standard Bouncy Castle (BC) libraries to their FIPS-certified counterparts (BC-FIPS), enabling a path toward FIPS 140-2/140-3 compliance. This includes a complete refactoring of PemUtils to use BC libraries for PEM file parsing.

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- **BC to BC-FIPS Migration**: All Bouncy Castle libraries replaced with FIPS-certified versions:
  - `bc-fips` 2.0.0 (core provider)
  - `bcpkix-fips` 2.0.7 (PKIX/CMS support)
  - `bctls-fips` 2.0.19 (TLS/JSSE provider)
  - `bcutil-fips` 2.0.3 (utilities)
  - `bcpg-fips` 2.0.10 (OpenPGP for plugin verification)
- **PemUtils Refactoring**: Complete rewrite using BC's PEMParser for handling various key formats
- **New java.security Configuration**: Security provider configuration for BC-FIPS
- **Enhanced Key Support**: PKCS#1, PKCS#8 (encrypted/unencrypted), EC, DSA formats
- **Increased Security Standards**: Higher key length requirements, improved Kerberos algorithms

### Summary
This release item covers four bug fixes for the Apache HttpClient 5.x transport layer in OpenSearch v3.0.0:

1. **JDK 16+ Protocol Version Fix** - Resolves `ParseException: Invalid protocol version` errors by adding a custom `TlsDetailsFactory` to properly extract application protocol from SSL engine
2. **H2C Compression Support** - Fixes Netty pipeline configuration for HTTP/2 cleartext protocol upgrade where compression handlers were incorrectly ordered
3. **Memory Allocation Optimization** - Prevents `HeapBufferedAsyncEntityConsumer` from over-allocating response buffers (up to 100MB default) regardless of actual response size
4. **HTTP/2 Protocol Version** - Adds `HTTP_2_0` enum value to `HttpRequest.HttpVersion` for proper HTTP/2 request identification

### Key Changes in v3.0.0
- Fixed TLS negotiation with JDK 16+ by implementing proper application protocol extraction
- Corrected Netty handler ordering for h2c compression (decoder_compress before aggregator)
- Changed buffer allocation strategy from pre-allocating max limit to allocating based on actual content length
- Extended HttpVersion enum to support HTTP/2.0 protocol identification

This feature adds support for remote indexes and multiple indexes in anomaly detection. The implementation enables anomaly detectors to use data from remote clusters via cross-cluster search and to monitor multiple indexes simultaneously.

- Feature report: `docs/features/flow-framework/flow-framework-access-control.md` (created)

### Summary
Flow Framework Access Control adds user-level security for workflow resources based on backend roles. When enabled via `plugins.flow_framework.filter_by_backend_roles`, users can only access workflows created by users who share at least one backend role.

### Key Changes in v2.17.0
- New cluster setting `plugins.flow_framework.filter_by_backend_roles` (default: false)
- All workflow APIs (create, update, delete, provision, deprovision, reprovision, get, search) now support backend role filtering
- New `SearchHandler` class for centralized search filtering
- New utility methods in `ParseUtils` for permission checking
- Users without backend roles are blocked from creating workflows when filtering is enabled

- Support for ingesting from multiple files with cross-file field mapping
- New connector action types: `CANCEL_BATCH_PREDICT` and `BATCH_PREDICT_STATUS`

- Feature report: `docs/features/k-nn/k-nn-query-rescore.md`

### Summary
The k-NN Query Rescore feature enables a two-phase search approach for quantized vector indexes. In the first phase, an oversampled set of candidates is retrieved using approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search with quantized vectors. In the second phase, full-precision vectors are loaded from disk to recompute exact distances, improving recall while maintaining memory efficiency.

### Key Changes in v2.17.0
- Two-phase search approach: oversample with ANN, then rescore with exact search
- New `rescore` parameter in k-NN query with configurable `oversample_factor` (1.0-100.0)
- New components: `RescoreContext`, `ExactSearcher`, `ResultUtil`
- Support for nested field searches with rescoring
- Default rescoring behavior based on compression level for `on_disk` mode

OpenSearch 2.17.0 introduces byte vector support for the Faiss engine, enabling significant memory savings (up to 75%) for vector search applications. This feature allows vectors with signed 8-bit integer values (-128 to 127) to be indexed and searched using both HNSW and IVF algorithms.

- **New components**: `ByteIndexService`, `ByteTrainingDataConsumer`, `BinaryTrainingDataConsumer`

- Memory reduction: up to 72-75%
- Indexing throughput: 13-107% improvement
- Recall reduction: 1-9% depending on dataset

### Summary
Disk-based vector search is a new k-NN feature introduced in v2.17.0 that enables efficient vector search in low-memory environments. It uses binary quantization to compress vectors (up to 32x compression) and a two-phase search approach with automatic rescoring to maintain high recall.

### Key Changes in v2.17.0

- New `compression_level` parameter supporting x1, x2, x8, x16, x32 compression
- Online binary quantization (no pretraining required)
- Two-phase search with automatic rescoring
- Default 32x compression for on_disk mode
- Automatic oversample factor configuration based on compression level

### Summary
The Flint Query Scheduler introduces an external scheduling mechanism for managing automatic index refreshes in OpenSearch's async query feature. It integrates with the OpenSearch Job Scheduler plugin to provide cost-effective, observable, and controllable refresh operations for Flint indexes (skipping indexes, covering indexes, and materialized views) used with external data sources like Amazon S3.

### Key Changes in v2.17.0
- **Job Scheduler Plugin Integration**: SQLPlugin now extends JobSchedulerExtension, enabling scheduled job management
- **Async Query Scheduler Service**: Abstract `AsyncQueryScheduler` interface with `OpenSearchAsyncQueryScheduler` implementation
- **Feature Flag Support**: Configuration option `plugins.query.executionengine.async_query.enabled` to enable/disable the scheduler
- **New System Index**: `.async-query-scheduler` for storing scheduled job metadata
- **Flint Operations Integration**: DROP, VACUUM, and ALTER operations automatically manage scheduler jobs

### Key Changes in v2.17.0
- **Job Scheduler Plugin Integration**: SQLPlugin now extends JobSchedulerExtension, enabling scheduled job management
- **Async Query Scheduler Service**: Abstract `AsyncQueryScheduler` interface with `OpenSearchAsyncQueryScheduler` implementation
- **Feature Flag Support**: Configuration option `plugins.query.executionengine.async_query.enabled` to enable/disable the scheduler
- **New System Index**: `.async-query-scheduler` for storing scheduled job metadata
- **Flint Operations Integration**: DROP, VACUUM, and ALTER operations automatically manage scheduler jobs

### Summary
Query Shape Generation in v2.17.0 introduces the ability to group similar Top N queries by their structural similarity. This addresses the problem where duplicate expensive queries can spam all Top N slots, preventing visibility into other expensive query patterns.

### Key Changes in v2.17.0
- **QueryShapeGenerator**: Generates normalized query shape strings from search requests (query, aggregations, sort)
- **MinMaxHeapQueryGrouper**: Efficient grouping using min/max heap algorithm for Top N tracking
- **Measurement class**: Supports aggregation types (NONE, SUM, AVERAGE) for grouped metrics
- **New settings**: `search.insights.top_queries.group_by` (similarity/none) and `max_groups_excluding_topn`

### Summary
This investigation covered four security authentication enhancements introduced in OpenSearch v2.17.0 across the security plugin and security-dashboards-plugin repositories.

### Key Changes in v2.17.0

1. **Multiple JWT Signing Keys** (security#4632, #4666)
   - Support for configuring multiple JWT signing keys as a list

   - Requests without proxy headers redirect to standard login page

   - New `ignore_hosts` configuration for auth failure listeners
   - Allows excluding trusted IPs/hostnames from rate limiting
   - Supports wildcard patterns and hostname matching
   - Partially resolves issue #4262

4. **Improved Redirect URL Handling** (security-dashboards-plugin#2072)
   - Uses core `getRedirectUrl` utility for consistent redirect behavior
   - Improves SAML and OpenID Connect authentication flows

### Summary
The k-NN Iterative Graph Build feature introduced in v2.17.0 enables memory-optimized index construction for FAISS-based k-NN indexes. Instead of loading all vectors into memory before building the graph, vectors are transferred and indexed in batches, significantly reducing peak memory consumption during indexing operations.

### Key Changes in v2.17.0
- Integrates FAISS iterative graph builds with `NativeEngines990KnnVectorsFormat`
- Introduces new JNI methods: `initIndex`, `insertToIndex`, `writeIndex` for three-phase index creation
- Adds `MemOptimizedNativeIndexBuildStrategy` for memory-efficient FAISS index building
- Adds `OffHeapVectorTransfer` classes for batch vector transfer to off-heap memory
- Refactors `NativeIndexWriter` to select appropriate build strategy based on engine type

   - Fixed `dataSourceId` not appearing in URL on Overview landing page
   - Corrected condition check in `AnomalyDetectionOverview.tsx`

### Summary
OpenSearch v2.18.0 upgrades Apache Lucene from 9.11.1 to 9.12.0, bringing significant performance improvements and new features to the search engine core.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- **Lucene 9.12.0 Upgrade**: Updates the underlying search library from 9.11.1 to 9.12.0
- **New Lucene912PostingsFormat**: Default postings format now uses 2-level skip data inlined into postings, improving performance for conjunction queries
- **JDK 23 Support**: Panama Vectorization Provider now supports JDK 23
- **Dynamic Range Facets**: New faceting feature that automatically picks balanced numeric ranges based on value distribution
- **Search Concurrency Configuration**: TieredMergePolicy and LogMergePolicy now support configurable search concurrency
- **Memory Optimizations**: Reduced memory allocations and improved heap usage for HNSW and scalar quantized vector writers
- **OnHeapHnswGraph Optimization**: No longer allocates a lock for every graph node
- **Shared Arena Improvements**: Files from the same segment can be grouped to a single shared Arena to reduce performance degradation

### Reports Created
- Release report: `docs/releases/v2.18.0/features/neural-search/neural-search-reranking.md`
- Feature report: `docs/features/neural-search/neural-search-reranking.md`

### Summary
OpenSearch v2.18.0 introduces two significant reranking enhancements for neural search:

1. **ByFieldRerankProcessor** - A new `by_field` rerank type that allows reranking search results based on a numeric field value stored in the document's `_source`. This is useful when ML models have pre-computed relevance scores or when business logic requires reordering by specific field values.

2. **Hybrid Query Rescorer** - Enables standard OpenSearch rescore functionality within hybrid queries. Previously, rescore queries were ignored when used with hybrid queries. This fix applies rescorers at the shard level before score normalization.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- New `by_field` rerank type with `target_field`, `remove_target_field`, and `keep_previous_score` configuration options
- Hybrid query now properly processes rescore queries at shard level
- Rescore scores are applied before normalization (final scores typically in 0-1 range)

- Feature report: `docs/features/k-nn/k-nn-avx512-support.md`

### Summary
OpenSearch v2.18.0 adds AVX512 SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data) support to the k-NN plugin for the Faiss engine. This enhancement accelerates vector search and indexing operations on x64 processors that support AVX512 instructions.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- Added AVX512 SIMD instruction support for the Faiss library
- Introduced new native library `libopensearchknn_faiss_avx512.so` optimized for AVX512
- Added automatic runtime detection and loading of the appropriate SIMD-optimized library
- New cluster setting `knn.faiss.avx512.disabled` to control AVX512 usage
- Updated build system to support AVX512 compilation flags (`-Davx512.enabled`, `-DAVX512_ENABLED`)

### Performance Ranking
AVX512 > AVX2 > No optimization

AVX512 processes 512 bits (16 floats) per operation compared to AVX2's 256 bits (8 floats), potentially doubling throughput for distance calculations.

OpenSearch v2.18.0 introduces significant enhancements to the Query Insights plugin focused on operational monitoring, query grouping accuracy, and historical data retrieval.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0

1. **Health Stats API** (`/_insights/health_stats`)
   - New endpoint for monitoring plugin health per node
   - Returns thread pool info, query records queue size, and top queries health stats

2. **OpenTelemetry Error Metrics**
   - Error counters for observability: `LOCAL_INDEX_EXPORTER_BULK_FAILURES`, `LOCAL_INDEX_EXPORTER_EXCEPTIONS`, `DATA_INGEST_EXCEPTIONS`, `QUERY_CATEGORIZE_EXCEPTIONS`, etc.

   - Field name and type support for more accurate query grouping
   - Default values changed from `false` to `true` for `field_name` and `field_type` settings
   - Query shapes now include field types (e.g., `match [name, text]`, `range [age, integer]`)

4. **Historical Query Retrieval**
   - Time range parameters (`from`/`to`) for querying historical top N queries from local index
   - Example: `GET /_insights/top_queries?from=2024-08-25T15:00:00.000Z&to=2024-08-30T17:00:00.000Z`

5. **Cache Management**
   - Index field type cache with eviction logic
   - Cluster state listener for invalidating cache on index deletion/update

### Summary
This release fixes a bug in `ReprovisionWorkflowTransportAction` where the template update was occurring at the wrong location in the execution flow, causing flaky integration tests.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- Fixed template update location to occur at the start of workflow execution rather than after completion
- Resolved race condition that caused `testReprovisionWorkflow` integration test to fail intermittently
- Improved logger statements to include workflow step type for better debugging

### Technical Details
The original implementation updated the template document after all workflow steps completed successfully. This created a race condition where the workflow state could be checked before the template was fully updated. The fix moves the template update to the beginning of the async execution, ensuring the template is updated before workflow steps are processed.

### Summary
Workload Management (WLM) is a comprehensive feature for tenant-level admission control and reactive query management. It enables system administrators to group search traffic into query groups with defined resource limits (CPU, memory), preventing resource overuse and ensuring fair distribution across the cluster.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- **QueryGroup resource cancellation framework** - Core mechanism for canceling queries exceeding resource limits
- **QueryGroup Stats API** - New `GET /_wlm/stats` endpoint for monitoring query group metrics
- **WLM resiliency orchestrator** - Query Sandboxing service (QueryGroupService) for enforcing resource limits
- **QueryGroup persistence** - Query groups are now durable across cluster restarts via ClusterState
- **Enhanced rejection mechanism** - Improved rejection logic for soft query groups when nodes are in duress
- **REST API bug fixes** - Fixed CRUD APIs to properly extend TransportClusterManagerNodeAction

- Feature report: `docs/features/opensearch/cluster-state-management.md` (updated)

### Summary
This PR (#15424) adds a fallback mechanism for cluster state retrieval when there's a term-version mismatch between nodes. In large clusters (1000+ nodes), cluster state appliers may take significant time (~18 seconds) to commit the cluster state. During this period, read requests would previously fetch the entire cluster state from the cluster manager.

The new mechanism provides three fallback sources:
1. **Applied State**: The locally committed cluster state (existing behavior)
2. **Pre-commit State**: The cluster state that has been published but not yet applied locally
3. **Remote Cluster State**: Download from remote storage when remote publication is enabled

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- New `RemoteClusterStateCache` component for caching downloaded cluster state by term-version
- New `preCommitState` atomic reference in `ClusterApplierService` storing published but uncommitted state
- New `isStatePresentInRemote` field in `GetTermVersionResponse` indicating remote availability
- New feature flag `opensearch.experimental.optimization.termversion.precommit.enabled`
- Modified `TransportClusterManagerNodeAction` with `getStateFromLocalNode()` fallback logic

- Feature report: `docs/features/opensearch/tiered-caching.md` (updated)

### Summary
PR #16047 introduces segmented cache architecture to the tiered spillover cache, significantly improving performance for concurrent read/write operations. The change addresses critical performance issues where a single global read/write lock created a bottleneck.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- **Segmented Cache Architecture**: Cache divided into multiple segments (default based on CPU cores), each with its own read/write lock
- **Improved Concurrency**: Multiple writers can operate simultaneously on different segments
- **Query Recomputation Outside Lock**: Cache miss handling no longer blocks other threads during query recomputation
- **New Configuration Settings**:
  - `indices.requests.cache.tiered_spillover.segments` - Number of cache segments (power of 2, up to 256)
  - `indices.requests.cache.tiered_spillover.onheap.store.size` - On-heap cache size
  - `indices.requests.cache.tiered_spillover.disk.store.size` - Disk cache size

### Summary
Star-tree index is an experimental feature introduced in OpenSearch v2.18.0 that precomputes aggregations during indexing. It significantly reduces query latency for aggregation queries by storing precomputed results in a hierarchical tree structure, enabling sub-millisecond query latency even on datasets with hundreds of millions of documents.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- Initial experimental release of star-tree index
- Support for metric aggregations: sum, min, max, avg, value_count

## Investigation Complete

### Reports Created
- Release report: `docs/releases/v2.18.0/features/opensearch/cluster-state-management.md`
- Feature report: `docs/features/opensearch/cluster-state-management.md` (created)

### Summary
This PR fixes a bug in cluster state management where the committed voting configuration could become stale during remote cluster state publication. The issue occurs because:

1. When voting configuration changes, the accepted configuration is sent during publish phase
2. Follower nodes apply this on `lastSeenClusterState`
3. In commit phase, nodes set committed config from accepted config
4. Next cluster state update (without voting config diff) applies diff on stale `lastSeenClusterState`
5. This causes committed voting configuration to retain older values

The fix updates `lastSeenClusterState` in the commit phase to ensure subsequent diffs are applied on the correct base state.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- Added `Consumer<ClusterState> updateLastSeen` parameter to `Coordinator.handleApplyCommit()`
- Changed `PublicationTransportHandler` handler from `BiConsumer` to `TriConsumer`
- Added `updateLastSeen()` method in `PublicationTransportHandler` to update `lastSeenClusterState`

### Summary
Fixed a critical race condition in the node-join and node-left processing loop that could prevent nodes from rejoining the cluster indefinitely. The fix introduces a pending disconnection tracking mechanism in `ClusterConnectionManager` that rejects join requests from nodes with ongoing node-left tasks.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- Added `pendingDisconnections` set in `ClusterConnectionManager` to track nodes with ongoing node-left tasks
- Nodes are marked as pending disconnect before cluster state publish phase
- Join requests from pending disconnect nodes are rejected with `IllegalStateException`
- Pending disconnections are cleared after commit or on cluster manager failover
- Added integration tests (`NodeJoinLeftIT`) to verify the fix

### Summary
This release item introduces experimental support for user-level personal settings in OpenSearch Dashboards. The feature allows individual users to customize their dashboard preferences without affecting other users' configurations.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- **User Settings Page**: New dedicated page for users to configure personal preferences
- **Scoped UI Settings**: Settings can now be defined with `scope: 'user'` to indicate user-level storage
- **User ID Translation**: `UserUISettingsClientWrapper` translates `<current_user>` placeholders to actual usernames
- **Permission Control**: When ACL is enabled, user settings are protected with user-specific permissions
- **API Support**: REST endpoints support `?scope=user` query parameter for user-scoped operations

### Technical Details
- New `UiSettingScope` enum with `GLOBAL` and `USER` values
- Modified `IUiSettingsClient` interface to accept optional scope parameter
- User settings stored as saved objects with type `config` and id as username
- Requires authentication to be enabled for user-level settings to work

### Summary
Async Query is a feature in OpenSearch Dashboards v2.18.0 that enables asynchronous execution of queries against external data sources like Amazon S3. It provides frontend polling mechanisms to handle long-running queries without timeout issues.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- **Frontend Polling**: Moved polling logic from backend to frontend to prevent timeout issues for queries taking 1-2 minutes
- **Async PPL Support**: Added `pplasync` search strategy enabling PPL queries for S3 datasets
- **New Components**: `ppl_async_search_strategy.ts`, `handleQueryResults` helper, `IDataFramePollingResponse` type
- **Default Query Update**: Changed default PPL query to `source = ${dataset.title} | head 10`

### Summary
The Query Editor feature in OpenSearch Dashboards v2.18.0 includes three key improvements:

1. **Footer Bar for Single-Line Editor** - A new footer bar appears when the single-line query editor is focused, displaying line count, timestamp field name, query execution status, and a recent queries button.

2. **Query Editor Extension Ordering Fix** - Fixed an issue where query editor extensions were not rendering in the correct order due to asynchronous React portal creation within the same container.

3. **PPL Autocomplete Improvements** - Fixed various issues with PPL autocomplete including function suggestions (aggregate functions), field and table name suggestions, and improved keyword sorting/display.

### Key Changes in v2.18.0
- Added `queryEditor__footer` component with start/end item slots
- Created separate pre-ordered containers for each query editor extension
- Added aggregate function suggestions (avg, count, sum, min, max, var_samp, var_pop, stddev_samp, stddev_pop)
- Improved error handling to properly surface errors from async search strategies
- Keywords now display in lowercase for better readability

### Summary
Hybrid Query Collapse is a highly requested feature (21 +1 reactions on Issue #665) that enables result deduplication in hybrid search by grouping results based on a field value. The implementation includes:

- **Collapse functionality**: Group results by `keyword` or numeric field, returning only the highest-scoring document per unique value
- **Performance improvement**: Custom bulk scorer achieving 2-3x faster hybrid query execution
- **RRF custom weights**: Support for custom weights in RRF normalization technique (must sum to 1.0)
- **Full integration**: Works with sort, explain, and pagination

- PR #1289: Custom bulk scorer with window-based collection (2-3x performance improvement)
- PR #1322: Support custom weights in RRF normalization processor

New collapse package with strategy pattern:
- `CollapseDTO`, `CollapseDataCollector`, `CollapseExecutor`
- `CollapseStrategy` (keyword and numeric strategies)
- `HybridCollapsingTopDocsCollector`

- Feature report: `docs/features/security/resource-access-control-framework.md` (created)

### Summary
The Resource Access Control Framework introduces centralized, fine-grained access management for plugin-defined resources in OpenSearch. It enables document-level authorization for higher-level objects such as ML models, anomaly detectors, and reports, replacing the legacy backend-role-based access model with owner-controlled sharing capabilities.

### Key Changes in v3.1.0
- **Centralized Resource Sharing SPI**: New `opensearch-security-spi` package that plugins implement via `ResourceSharingExtension` interface
- **1:1 Backing Sharing Indices**: Each resource index now has a dedicated sharing index (e.g., `.plugins-ml-model-group` → `.plugins-ml-model-group-sharing`)
- **Automatic Access Evaluation**: `ResourceAccessEvaluator` automatically evaluates access permissions via Security Filter
- **Owner-Controlled Sharing**: Resource owners can share/revoke access with specific users, roles, or backend roles
- **Java APIs**: `verifyResourceAccess()`, `share()`, `revoke()`, `getAccessibleResourceIds()` for plugins

- PR: [#5281](https://github.com/opensearch-project/security/pull/5281) - Centralized Resource Access Control Framework

OpenSearch v3.1.0 significantly expands the Calcite-based PPL engine with support for 15+ new commands and functions. This release adds window functions (`eventstats`), data transformation commands (`flatten`, `expand`, `appendcol`), text processing (`grok`), aggregation commands (`top`, `rare`, `fillnull`), and performance optimizations including LIMIT pushdown and row count estimation.

### Key Changes in v3.1.0

**New PPL Commands:**
- `eventstats` - Window functions (avg, count, sum, min, max, var_samp, var_pop, stddev_samp, stddev_pop)
- `flatten` - Flatten nested struct/object fields into separate fields
- `expand` - Expand array fields into multiple rows
- `trendline` - Calculate trend lines over time-series data
- `appendcol` - Append columns from subquery results
- `grok` - Parse text using Grok patterns
- `top` / `rare` - Find most/least common values with count display options
- `fillnull` - Replace null values with specified defaults
- `describe` - Show index metadata and field information
- `patterns` - Pattern detection using BRAIN method

- `isempty`, `isblank`, `ispresent` - String/field validation
- `geoip` - GeoIP lookup for IP addresses
- `cidrmatch` - Check if IP matches CIDR range

- LIMIT pushdown to OpenSearch for reduced data transfer
- Row count estimation for improved query planning
- ResourceMonitor for memory monitoring in CalciteEnumerableIndexScan

### Summary
OpenSearch v3.1.0 introduces enhanced security cache management capabilities with two key improvements:

1. **Selective User Cache Invalidation**: A new REST endpoint `DELETE /_plugins/_security/api/cache/user/{username}` allows administrators to invalidate authentication cache entries for individual users without affecting other cached entries.

2. **Dynamic Cache TTL Configuration**: The `plugins.security.cache.ttl_minutes` setting can now be updated dynamically via the cluster settings API without requiring a cluster restart.

### Key Changes in v3.1.0
- New endpoint for per-user cache invalidation addresses inefficiency of global cache flush
- Particularly useful for LDAP environments where user backend roles may change
- Dynamic TTL changes are transient (not persisted across restarts)
- Cache invalidation requires admin TLS certificate authentication

### Reports Created
- Release report: `docs/releases/v3.1.0/features/security/security-performance-improvements.md`
- Feature report: `docs/features/security/security-performance-improvements.md`

### Summary
This enhancement introduces significant performance improvements to the OpenSearch security layer through an immutable User object implementation. The changes reduce serialization overhead during inter-node communication by enabling caching of serialized data and deserialized User objects.

### Key Changes in v3.1.0
- **Immutable User Object**: The `User` class is now immutable, using builder-style methods (`withRoles()`, `withAttributes()`, etc.) instead of mutable setters
- **Serialization Caching**: Serialized binary data is computed once per User object and reused across requests
- **Deserialization Caching**: `UserFactory.Caching` maps serialized data to User objects, reducing deserialization operations
- **Thread Safety**: Immutable objects eliminate synchronization overhead
- **New Interfaces**: `AuthenticationContext` for passing data between auth backends, `ImpersonationBackend` for user impersonation support
- **Configurable Cache**: New settings `plugins.security.user_cache.max_size` and `plugins.security.user_cache.expire_after_access`

### Performance Improvements
- Users with 10 attributes: 21% throughput improvement
- Users with 100 attributes: 39% throughput improvement

### Resources Used
- PR: [#5339](https://github.com/opensearch-project/security/pull/5339) - Remove unused custom User serialization
- PR: [#5212](https://github.com/opensearch-project/security/pull/5212) - Immutable user object

## Investigation Complete

### Reports Created
- Release report: `docs/releases/v3.1.0/features/security/security-permissions.md`
- Feature report: `docs/features/security/security-permissions.md`

### Summary
This release item adds missing security permissions for the Forecasting plugin in OpenSearch v3.1.0. Three PRs addressed permission gaps:

1. **PR #5386**: Added `forecast_read_access` and `forecast_full_access` roles with complete permissions for the forecasting feature
2. **PR #5405**: Added missing `cluster_monitor` permission required for cross-cluster forecaster creation
3. **PR #5412**: Added missing `indices:admin/mappings/get` permission for index mapping retrieval

### Key Changes in v3.1.0
- New `forecast_read_access` role with read-only permissions for forecast resources
- New `forecast_full_access` role with full permissions including:
  - `cluster:admin/plugin/forecast/*` for all forecast operations
  - `cluster_monitor` for cluster monitoring (cross-cluster support)
  - `indices:admin/mappings/get` for mapping retrieval
  - Various index permissions for data read/write operations

### Resources Used
- PR: [#5386](https://github.com/opensearch-project/security/pull/5386), [#5405](https://github.com/opensearch-project/security/pull/5405), [#5412](https://github.com/opensearch-project/security/pull/5412)
- Docs: [Security Permissions](https://docs.opensearch.org/3.0/security/access-control/permissions/)
- Related: [Security Dashboards Plugin PR #2253](https://github.com/opensearch-project/security-dashboards-plugin/pull/2253)

Parallel Shard Refresh is an experimental feature that enables individual shards within an index to refresh independently rather than at the index level. ### Summary
Derived Source is a storage optimization feature that eliminates the need to store the `_source` field during document ingestion. Instead of duplicating data, OpenSearch dynamically reconstructs documents from `doc_values` and stored fields on demand. This can reduce storage costs by up to 2x while maintaining full search functionality.

### Key Changes in v3.1.0
- Added `DerivedFieldGenerator` class for generating source from field storage
- Implemented `FieldValueFetcher` base class with specialized fetchers:
  - `SortedNumericDocValuesFetcher` for numeric doc values
  - `SortedSetDocValuesFetcher` for keyword/IP doc values
  - `StoredFieldFetcher` for stored fields
- Support for 10+ field types: Date, Number, Boolean, IP, Keyword, Text, Geo Point, Constant Keyword, Scaled Float, Wildcard

OpenSearch v3.1.0 introduces two significant query optimization improvements:

1. **BooleanQuery Rewrite for must_not RangeQuery Clauses** - Automatically transforms slow `must_not` range queries into faster `should` clauses representing the complement of the range. This achieves 2-30x performance improvements depending on the query pattern.

### Summary
System Ingest Pipeline is a new capability in OpenSearch 3.1 that enables plugin developers to automatically process documents during ingestion based on index mappings. Unlike standard ingest pipelines that require manual user configuration, system ingest pipelines are automatically generated by OpenSearch based on registered system ingest processor factories.

### Key Changes in v3.1.0
- **Automatic Pipeline Generation**: OpenSearch generates pipelines based on index mappings and registered processor factories
- **Plugin Developer API**: New `AbstractBatchingSystemProcessor` base class and `SystemIngestProcessor.Factory` for creating custom system processors
- **Bulk Update Support**: System pipelines are applied to all update operations including bulk updates (PR #18277)
- **Pipeline Caching**: System ingest pipelines are cached per index (max 100 entries, 60 min TTL) with automatic invalidation on mapping changes
- **Cluster Setting**: New `cluster.ingest.system_pipeline_enabled` setting (default: `true`) to enable/disable system pipelines
- **Execution Order**: System pipelines execute after default and final pipelines

### Summary
The Approximation Framework Enhancement in v3.1.0 updates the BKD tree traversal logic to improve performance on skewed datasets. The key improvement is switching from a BFS-like traversal to a DFS-based strategy that enables early termination when collecting top-N results.

### Key Changes in v3.1.0
- **DFS-based traversal**: Replaced BFS-like traversal with depth-first search that naturally produces results in sorted order
- **Smart child skipping**: Added logic to skip subtrees when the current subtree contains enough documents to satisfy the query

### Summary
This investigation covered two critical bug fixes for snapshot and repository operations in OpenSearch v3.1.0:

1. **Infinite Loop Prevention** (PR #17532): Fixed a race condition where updating a repository while a snapshot creation is in progress could cause the snapshot operation to enter an infinite loop. - Added `closed` flag to `BlobStoreRepository` to detect repository closure during snapshot operations
- Changed `isRemoteStoreIndexShallowCopyEnabled()` check to use null-safe `Boolean.TRUE.equals()` pattern
- Snapshot operations now fail gracefully with `RepositoryException` when repository is updated during snapshot creation

### Summary
The `DocRequest` interface is a new abstraction introduced in OpenSearch v3.1.0 that provides a generic way to categorize ActionRequests that operate on a single document. This refactoring creates a cleaner hierarchy for document-related requests and serves as the foundation for the Security plugin's resource-level access control feature.

### Key Changes in v3.1.0
- New `DocRequest` interface with `index()`, `id()`, and `type()` methods
- `DocWriteRequest` now extends `DocRequest` (previously standalone)
- `GetRequest` now implements `DocRequest`
- Enables plugins to implement fine-grained resource sharing (Google Docs-style access control)

### Summary
OpenSearch v3.2.0 introduces two new utility classes to the Flow Framework plugin for JSON-to-JSON transformation:

1. **JsonToJsonRecommender**: Analyzes input/output JSON pairs and automatically generates JSONPath mapping recommendations. Builds an inverted index from input values to paths, then correlates with output structure to produce both detailed (explicit indices) and generalized (wildcard `[*]`) mappings.

2. **JsonToJsonTransformer**: Transforms input JSON into target structure using JSONPath mapping rules. Supports explicit indices and wildcard patterns for array processing.

### Key Changes in v3.2.0
- New `JsonToJsonRecommender` utility class for automated JSON field mapping inference
- New `JsonToJsonTransformer` utility class for JSON structure transformation using JSONPath
- Support for both detailed (explicit array indices) and generalized (`[*]` wildcards) mappings
- Configurable limits: ~50MB max JSON size, 1000 max nesting depth, 50000 max key length

### Summary
OpenSearch v3.2.0 introduces two new ISM transition conditions that enable more expressive lifecycle policies:

1. **`no_alias` (boolean)**: Gates transitions based on alias presence
   - `true`: Transition only if the index has no aliases
   - `false`: Transition only if the index has at least one alias

2. **`min_state_age` (duration)**: Allows transitions only after an index has spent a minimum time in its current ISM state
   - Addresses the limitation of `min_index_age` which measures time since index creation
   - Enables accurate state-specific retention periods

Additionally, the ISM history index pattern (`.opendistro-ism-managed-index-history*`) is now registered as a System Index descriptor.

### Summary
This enhancement improves error handling in ML Commons by returning proper HTTP 400 (Bad Request) errors instead of HTTP 500 (Internal Server Error) for invalid client inputs. This follows REST API best practices by distinguishing between client errors (4xx) and server errors (5xx).

### Summary
This release item introduces two performance optimizations to the OpenSearch security layer:

1. **Precomputed Privileges Toggle** (`plugins.security.privileges_evaluation.precomputed_privileges.enabled`)
   - Allows disabling denormalized privilege data structures
   - Useful for clusters with many roles and repeated index patterns where initialization takes excessive time
   - Enabled by default for backward compatibility

2. **Optimized Wildcard Matching**
   - New `PrefixMatcher` for `prefix*` patterns using `String.startsWith()`
   - New `ContainsMatcher` for `*contains*` patterns using `String.contains()`
   - ~30% performance improvement for common wildcard patterns

### Key Changes in v3.2.0
- New setting to disable precomputed privileges when initialization overhead is problematic
- Specialized wildcard matchers for common patterns (prefix and contains)
- Improved API for case-insensitive matching via `ignoreCase()` method

### Summary
This enhancement restricts star-tree index query optimization for users with Document-Level Security (DLS), Field-Level Security (FLS), or Field Masking restrictions. When these security restrictions are applied, queries automatically fall back to standard aggregation behavior to ensure data access controls are properly enforced.

### Key Changes in v3.2.0
- Star-tree query optimization is automatically disabled when DLS/FLS/Field Masking is active
- The `DlsFlsValveImpl.handleSearchContext()` method now checks for star-tree query context and sets it to null when restrictions apply
- Users without restrictions continue to benefit from star-tree acceleration
- No migration required - behavior change is automatic

This enhancement adds tenancy access level information to the serialized user context in the thread context. ### Summary
This release item adds support for composite indexes (star-tree indexes) in the custom-codecs plugin. Previously, custom codecs always delegated to `PerFieldMappingPostingFormatCodec`, which didn't support composite index features. Now, when an index has composite field mappings, the custom codecs properly delegate to `CompositeCodec`.

### Key Changes in v3.2.0
- Custom codecs now dynamically select the appropriate delegate codec based on `mapperService.isCompositeIndexPresent()`
- Codec constructors refactored to accept `Supplier<Codec>` instead of `MapperService` and `Logger`
- Enables combining custom compression (ZSTD, QAT hardware-accelerated) with star-tree index functionality

The Skills plugin v3.2.0 includes three key enhancements:

1. **Index Schema Merging for PPLTool**: When using index patterns (e.g., `logs-*`), PPLTool now merges schema metadata from all matching indexes instead of using only the first index's mapping. This ensures the LLM receives a complete view of all available fields.

2. **Error Message Masking**: PPLTool now masks sensitive information in error messages from SageMaker endpoints, including AWS account numbers, SageMaker ARNs, and CloudWatch URLs.

3. **Standardized Parameter Handling**: All Tool implementations now use the `extractInputParameters` utility from ML Commons, aligning with the unified tool parameter handling introduced in ML Commons PR #4053.

- New `MergeRule` interface and implementations (`DeepMergeRule`, `LatestRule`) for schema merging
- `redactSagemakerArns()` and `redactCloudwatchUrl()` methods for error masking
- Updated 12 tool classes to use `ToolUtils.extractInputParameters()`

This bugfix improves error handling in the Remote Vector Index Build feature. - Fixed by forcing `commons-beanutils:1.11.0` in build.gradle

**CVE-2025-7783 (dashboards-query-workbench)**
- Critical vulnerability in `form-data` npm package using predictable `Math.random()` for boundary selection
- Fixed by updating `@cypress/request` to 3.0.9 which includes `form-data` 4.0.4

### Resources Used
- PR: `https://github.com/opensearch-project/ml-commons/pull/4062`
- PR: `https://github.com/opensearch-project/dashboards-query-workbench/pull/503`
- Advisory: [GHSA-fjxv-7rqg-78g4](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fjxv-7rqg-78g4)

### Note
The original issue referenced PRs #270, #309 (query), and #756 (flow) which could not be found or did not match the CVE descriptions. The actual CVE fixes were identified through GitHub search and advisory references.

### Summary
OpenSearch 3.2.0 introduces four new routing processors that enable intelligent document co-location:

1. **HierarchicalRoutingProcessor** (ingest) - Routes documents based on hierarchical path structures using configurable anchor depth
2. **HierarchicalRoutingSearchProcessor** (search) - Automatically extracts path prefixes from queries to set search routing

4. **AclRoutingSearchProcessor** (search) - Extracts ACL values from term/terms queries for search routing

- New `hierarchical_routing_search` search request processor for automatic path-based routing
- New `acl_routing` ingest processor for tenant/group-based document routing
- New `acl_routing_search` search request processor for ACL-aware query routing
- Both processor pairs use consistent MurmurHash3 hashing for routing value generation
- Supports `term`, `terms`, `prefix`, and `wildcard` queries for routing extraction

### Summary
OpenSearch v3.2.0 enhances warm indices with three key improvements:

1. **Write Block on Flood Watermark Breach** - Warm indices now automatically apply write blocks when the flood stage watermark is exceeded, preventing data loss from disk pressure
2. **Addressable Space-based FS Stats** - Warm nodes report filesystem statistics based on total addressable space (file cache × remote_data_ratio) instead of physical disk
3. **Resize Operation Restrictions** - Clone, shrink, and split operations are now explicitly disallowed on warm indices

- Resize operations (clone/shrink/split) blocked for warm indices
- Parameterized integration tests for close operations in remote store

### Summary
OpenSearch 3.2.0 extends the BooleanQuery `must_not` rewrite optimization to support numeric match, term, and terms queries. When a `must_not` clause contains these query types on numeric fields, OpenSearch automatically rewrites them to equivalent `should` clauses containing range queries that represent the mathematical complement.

- Extended `must_not` rewrite to numeric match, term, and terms queries
- Introduced `ComplementAwareQueryBuilder` interface for queries that can provide complement ranges
- Added `ComplementHelperUtils` utility class for constructing complement range queries
- Performance improvements up to **54x** for common exclusion patterns

### Summary
This feature introduces an extensibility mechanism for OpenSearch plugins to inject custom `QueryCollectorContext` during the Query Phase of search execution. - Added `QueryCollectorContextSpecFactory` interface for creating specs based on search context and query
- Added `QueryCollectorContextSpecRegistry` as a static registry for managing factories
- Added `QueryCollectorArguments` class for passing arguments to factories
- Extended `SearchPlugin` interface with `getCollectorContextSpecFactories()` method

### Performance Impact
Based on benchmarking with hybrid queries (noaa-semantic-search dataset):
- p50 latency: 11.83% improvement
- p90 latency: 16.22% improvement  
- p99 latency: 11.49% improvement

- `FetchProfileBreakdown` - Tracks timing for individual fetch operations
- `FetchProfileShardResult` - Holds fetch profile results for a shard

   - Allows injecting unique writer identifiers into remote store paths
   - Enables multiple writers to write to the same shard without conflicts
   - Path structure: `remote_repository/hash/index-uuid/shard-id/<path-prefix>/segments/data/file`

### Summary
OpenSearch v3.2.0 brings three significant enhancements to the Approximation Framework:

1. **`search_after` Support for Numeric Queries** - Enables efficient deep pagination while maintaining early termination benefits. For ASC sort, the `search_after` value becomes the new lower bound; for DESC sort, it becomes the upper bound.

2. **Range Queries with `now` in Date Fields** - Previously, range queries using `now` bypassed approximation due to `DateRangeIncludingNowQuery` wrapping. The query structure was refactored to ensure approximation is applied.

3. **Multiple Sort Fields Handling** - Approximation is now automatically disabled when queries use multiple sort fields to ensure result correctness (secondary sort fields are only applied after collection).

### Key Changes in v3.2.0
- New `NumericPointEncoder.encodePoint(Object, boolean)` API for `search_after` value encoding
- Modified `ApproximatePointRangeQuery` with `search_after` bound computation
- Restructured `DateRangeIncludingNowQuery` wrapping in `DateFieldMapper`
- Added multi-sort detection in `ApproximatePointRangeQuery` and `ApproximateMatchAllQuery`

### Performance Improvements
- `asc_sort_with_after_timestamp`: P90 latency reduced from ~194 ms to ~8 ms
- `desc_sort_with_after_timestamp`: P90 latency reduced from ~188 ms to ~7 ms

- Feature report: `docs/features/opensearch/numeric-terms-aggregation-optimization.md` (created)

### Summary
This optimization improves numeric terms aggregation performance by dynamically selecting the most efficient algorithm for top-N bucket selection. When the requested bucket size is large relative to total buckets, it uses quickselect instead of priority queue.

### Key Changes in v3.2.0
- New `BucketSelectionStrategy` enum with PRIORITY_QUEUE and QUICK_SELECT_OR_SELECT_ALL strategies
- Configurable `search.aggregation.bucket_selection_strategy_factor` setting (default: 5, range: 0-10)
- QuickSelect algorithm (via Lucene's `ArrayUtil.select()`) for top-N bucket selection
- Debug information exposed via profile API (`result_selection_strategy` field)

### Strategy Selection Logic
| Condition | Strategy |
|-----------|----------|
| `size * factor < bucketsInOrd` | PRIORITY_QUEUE |
| `isKeyOrder(order)` | PRIORITY_QUEUE |
| Significant terms aggregation | PRIORITY_QUEUE |
| Otherwise | QUICK_SELECT_OR_SELECT_ALL |

### Summary
This release optimizes the segment grouping algorithm for concurrent segment search. The new algorithm uses a priority queue to balance document counts across slices, replacing the previous round-robin distribution approach.

### Summary
This investigation covered three bug fixes for query string and regular expression queries in OpenSearch v3.2.0:

1. **Field Alias Support (PR #18215)**: Fixed `QueryStringQueryParser.getRegexpQuerySingle()` to use `currentFieldType.regexpQuery()` instead of delegating to Lucene's `super.getRegexpQuery()`, enabling proper field alias resolution.

- Regex queries in `query_string` now correctly resolve field aliases
- The `~` (COMPLEMENT) operator works again for regexp queries (deprecated, will be removed in OpenSearch 4.0)

This bugfix resolves an issue where system ingest pipelines were not triggered when index requests were forwarded from non-ingest nodes to ingest nodes.

### Key Changes in v3.2.0

- Added test coverage for cache miss scenario with forwarded requests

### Root Cause
When an index request arrives at a non-ingest node (e.g., dedicated master), the node resolves the pipeline and sets `isPipelineResolved = true`. When forwarded to an ingest node with an empty cache, the ingest node skipped pipeline resolution because the flag was already set.

### Summary
This feature adds support for leveraging user custom attributes in Alerting monitors. When a monitor is created or updated, the user's custom attributes are now saved with the monitor and passed to the Security plugin during monitor execution. This enables Document-Level Security (DLS) and Field-Level Security (FLS) queries that rely on parameter substitution with custom attributes to work correctly.

### Key Changes in v3.3.0
- Monitors now save user custom attributes (as `Map<String, String>`) when created/updated
- Custom attributes are passed to Security plugin via `InjectorContextElement` during monitor execution
- Enables DLS queries with parameter substitution (e.g., `${attr.internal.team}`) to work correctly
- Data model changed from `customAttNames` (List) to `customAttributes` (Map)

### Summary
OpenSearch v3.3.0 introduces significant enhancements to Snapshot Management (SM) in the Index Management plugin:

1. **Optional Creation Workflow**: The `creation` field in SM policies is now optional, enabling deletion-only policies. Previously, SM policies required both creation and deletion configurations.

2. **Snapshot Pattern Support**: A new `snapshot_pattern` field in the deletion configuration allows SM policies to include externally created snapshots in deletion workflows.

3. **ISM Snapshot Global State Fix**: The ISM snapshot action now excludes global state by default (`include_global_state: false`), preventing potential security issues when restoring snapshots.

### Key Changes in v3.3.0
- Made `creation` field optional in `SMPolicy` with version compatibility checks for backward compatibility
- Added `snapshotPattern` field to `SMPolicy.Deletion` for pattern-based snapshot matching
- Enhanced deletion states to combine policy-created and pattern-matched snapshots
- Applied deletion conditions (`max_age`, `min_count`) across all matching snapshots
- Added `snapshot_pattern` field to index mappings

### Use Cases Enabled
- **Cleanup-only workflows**: Delete old snapshots without automatic creation
- **External snapshot management**: Include snapshots created by external tools in retention policies
- **Flexible policy configurations**: Support creation-only, deletion-only, or combined workflows

### Summary
OpenSearch 3.3.0 introduces the `lateInteractionScore` function in the k-NN plugin, enabling ColBERT-style late interaction scoring for enhanced search relevance. This feature allows token-level matching between query and document vectors using the MaxSim (Maximum Similarity) scoring mechanism.

### Key Changes in v3.3.0

- Implements MaxSim algorithm: for each query vector, finds maximum similarity with any document vector and sums these maxima

- Enables two-phase search: fast k-NN retrieval followed by late interaction reranking

### Key Changes in v3.3.0
- **ScratchPad Tools**: New `WriteToScratchPadTool` and `ReadFromScratchPadTool` for intermediate state management during agent execution
- **Memory Architecture Refactoring**: Complete restructuring of the agentic memory system with Memory Containers, Working Memory, Long-Term Memory, and History tracking
- **Session Management API**: New API for creating and managing conversation sessions with custom or auto-generated IDs
- **GA Release**: Agentic memory feature enabled by default (`plugins.ml_commons.agentic_memory_enabled: true`)
- **Improved Fact Extraction**: Enhanced prompts with XML-based structure and JSON enforcement for better LLM compliance
- **Delete Control**: New `delete_all_memories` parameter for controlling cascade deletion behavior

### Summary

### Summary
SEISMIC (Spilled Clustering of Inverted Lists with Summaries for Maximum Inner Product Search) is a new approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) algorithm for sparse vectors introduced in OpenSearch 3.3. It enables billion-scale neural sparse search with sub-12ms query latency while maintaining 90%+ recall.

### Key Changes in v3.3.0
- New SEISMIC algorithm delivering 4x faster performance than BM25 and 10x faster than standard neural sparse search
- Custom Lucene codec with clustered posting lists and forward index caching
- Circuit breaker and memory stats for resource management (default 10% limit)
- Configurable quantization parameters (`quantization_ceiling_search`, `quantization_ceiling_ingest`)
- Index thread quantity setting API for controlling force merge parallelism
- Hybrid mode: segments below `approximate_threshold` use standard neural sparse query

- Feature report: `docs/features/sql/ppl-spath-command.md` (created)

### Summary
The `spath` command is a new PPL command introduced in v3.3.0 that provides a simple, intuitive way to extract fields from JSON data stored in text fields. It serves as a user-friendly alternative to the `json_extract()` function.

### Key Changes in v3.3.0
- New `spath` PPL command with syntax: `spath input=<field> [output=<field>] [path=]<path>`
- Supports nested field access (`parent.child`), array indexing (`list{0}`), and wildcard array access (`list{}`)
- Internally rewrites to `json_extract` eval expression for execution
- New AST node `SPath` and parser grammar extensions

### Technical Details
- Implementation is a lightweight conversion to `json_extract` function
- No pushdown optimization - extraction happens at coordinating node

This enhancement improves the Security plugin's health check API to include Authorization (AuthZ) initialization status. - Feature report: `docs/features/cross-cluster-replication/cross-cluster-replication.md` (updated)

### Summary
This release fixes a critical bug where replication of large documents could breach the 2GB size limit of `ReleasableBytesStreamOutput`, causing replication failures. The fix introduces dynamic batch size adjustment and a new index-level batch size setting.

### Key Changes in v3.3.0
- **New Setting**: `index.plugins.replication.follower.ops_batch_size` for index-level batch size control
- **Dynamic Batch Size Adjustment**: Automatically reduces batch size by half when 2GB limit is hit (minimum 16 operations)
- **Immediate Retry**: No delay when retrying after 2GB exception
- **New Component**: `BatchSizeSettings` helper class for managing batch size with fallback from index-level to cluster-level

### Technical Details
When the follower cluster fetches data from the leader node and the total size exceeds 2GB, the system now:
1. Detects the specific `ReleasableBytesStreamOutput cannot hold more than 2GB` exception
2. Reduces the batch size by half (minimum 16 operations)
3. Retries immediately without delay
4. Resets to original batch size after successful operations

### Summary
This bugfix resolves SSL/TLS compatibility issues between the Security plugin and the `transport-reactor-netty4` plugin. When using the reactor-netty4 transport (required for MCP server support and HTTP/2), the Security plugin failed to retrieve SSL information due to different naming conventions and classloader conflicts.

### Key Changes in v3.3.0
- Added fallback logic in Security plugin to use `ssl_engine` attribute when `ssl_handler` is unavailable
- Implemented `ReactorNetty4BaseHttpChannel` class to properly expose SSL attributes in reactor-netty4 transport
- Fixed classloader isolation issues by returning `SSLEngine` directly instead of `SslHandler`

**Query Execution Fixes:**
- count(*) and dc(field) now return bigint instead of integer to handle large datasets
- Fixed filter pushdown missing analyzed node for Search call
- Prevent limit pushdown before action building to avoid maxResultWindow issues
- Fixed ClassCastException for value-storing aggregates (first, last, min, max) on nested PPL fields

**Data Type and Function Fixes:**
- MOD function now returns decimal instead of float for decimal operands
- Fixed negative scale in decimal literals for Calcite engine
- parse/grok/patterns functions now return NULL instead of empty string for NULL input
- Fixed geopoint handling in complex data types

**Error Handling Improvements:**
- Missing index pattern now throws IndexNotFoundException
- Fixed alphanumeric search starting with number (PPL grammar fix)
- Fixed legacy JDBC type mapping inconsistency
- PPL Anonymizer now properly masks PPL queries

**CI/CD and Documentation:**
- Split test actions into unit, integ, and doctest
- Added spotless precommit hook + license check
- Enabled doctest with Calcite
- Updated documentation for bin, timechart, rex, coalesce, fields/table commands
- Added UDF/UDAF development guide
- Added Splunk comparison to PPL cheat sheet

### Reports Created
- Release report: `docs/releases/v3.3.0/features/opensearch/fetch-phase-profiling.md`
- Feature report: `docs/features/opensearch/profiler.md` (updated)

### Summary
OpenSearch v3.3.0 expands fetch phase profiling to support inner hits and top hits aggregation phases. Previously (v3.2.0), fetch phase profiling only supported the standard fetch phase. This enhancement provides complete visibility into all fetch operations, enabling developers to identify performance bottlenecks in complex queries involving nested documents and aggregations.

### Key Changes in v3.3.0
- Inner hits fetch operations are now profiled with descriptive labels (`fetch_inner_hits[<name>]`)
- Top hits aggregation fetch operations are now profiled with descriptive labels (`fetch_top_hits_aggregation[<name>]`)
- Multiple fetch operations of the same type are consolidated under a single breakdown entry
- Removed restriction in `FetchPhase.java` that limited profiling to standard fetch phase only

### Resources Used

This enhancement provides complete visibility into all fetch operations, enabling developers to identify performance bottlenecks in complex queries involving nested documents and aggregations.

- Inner hits fetch operations are now profiled with descriptive labels (`fetch_inner_hits[<name>]`)
- Top hits aggregation fetch operations are now profiled with descriptive labels (`fetch_top_hits_aggregation[<name>]`)
- Multiple fetch operations of the same type are consolidated under a single breakdown entry

### Summary
OpenSearch v3.3.0 introduces a comprehensive query rewriting infrastructure that automatically optimizes query structure before execution. The feature achieves 60-70% reduction in query nodes for typical filtered queries while preserving exact query semantics.

- New `QueryRewriterRegistry` singleton for managing rewriter chain execution
